question: Describe how observed relative solvent solubilities vary with temperature within the same training solute, recorded DOI and solvent pair. No primary LM hypothesis or causal mechanism is evaluated.
source_eligibility: Only explicit DOI strings matching ^10\.\d{4,9}/\S+$; report excluded missing/malformed DOI records. No source labels are corrected.
series: Full retained solute identity + exact recorded DOI + two ordered full solvent identities. Compare only temperatures where both solvents were measured; never interpolate or fabricate a measurement.
additional_summary: ALL temperature gaps; every bin and both relations retained including empty/insufficient groups.
conditional_metric: reversal_given_both_decisive is defined only when both measured differences exceed the preset near-tie band; report its support separately.
aggregation: Average temperature comparisons within each solute/DOI/solvent-pair series; average series within DOI; average DOIs within solute; macro mean over supported solutes, separately per relation/gap bin. Conditional metric skips undefined series/DOIs/solutes and reports support.

bootstrap.interval: percentile95%; descriptive conditional cohort uncertainty, not chemistry-wide or experimental noise uncertainty

strict_policy: Training predicate applied in Parquet before numerical labels are deserialized. No validation/test labels, LM predictions or scores used.
decision_policy: No retrieval-weight, threshold, prompt, candidate, method or checkpoint changes from this diagnostic. No stable/unstable classification threshold or hypothesis-support flag; retain all observed estimates.
limits: Temperature sampling and same-source pairs select a training-only subset.
pH, solid form, pressure and experimental-protocol differences can be unrecorded even within a DOI.
Within-solute order stability does not imply reliable transfer between different solutes.
Primary/strict training cohorts overlap and are not independent replications.
